summary: Backend-only testing of BUG FIX B (discover count/category) and Admin backup/restore. Added new pytest module /app/backend/tests/test_backup_and_discover.py (16 tests). All 16 pass on the shared preview backend, including RBAC (403 for non-super_admin), invalid body (400), count clamping [1..10], per-category discovery, association creating one device per thermostat, backup file existence, and full backup->restore roundtrip with admin login preservation.
critical_code_review_comments: The discover endpoint returns ALL current pending pairings for the installation (not just the newly-created batch). This is fine functionally, but the response semantics can be surprising for clients; consider returning only the newly inserted items or including a 'new_ids' field.

restore_backup performs delete_many + insert_many without a transaction; a mid-restore crash could leave the DB partially wiped. Consider wrapping in a Mongo transaction or writing to a shadow DB and swapping.
count is silently clamped to [1..10] rather than returning 400 for out-of-range values — acceptable but could hide client bugs.
test_credentials: admin@climazone.fr / Admin1234! ; client@demo.fr / Demo1234! ; installateur@demo.fr / Demo1234!
seed_data_creation: Created throwaway installation TEST_Discover_Install (installer) and associated 3 thermostats to new zones ZoneTest_0..2. Persistent but harmless.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backup/restore tests share the preview MongoDB with any other worker's tests, so restore_roundtrip briefly wipes and reinserts all BACKUP_COLLECTIONS. The test file uses -n 2 loadscope; _clear_pairing helper retries to survive this race. Run via: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_backup_and_discover.py -v. Backup file lives at /app/backend/data/backup.json.
rca of the issue: Original bug B (5 thermostats -> 1..3 discovered) was already fixed: the discover endpoint now accepts count (clamped 1..10) and category, and creates exactly `count` pairing docs before returning the full pending list. Verified via delta assertions (post-pre == count) for count in {1,3,5}, clamp verified for 0 and 50.
